entries.reason: ROLLOPS_PLUGIN_PUBLIC_KEY is operator configuration, not attacker-controlled input. VerifyArtifact reads it as the path to the cosign public key used to verify plugin signatures; whoever can set the process environment can already read any file the process can, so treating it as a path-traversal source assumes a threat model in which the attack is already unnecessary. Same shape as a --config flag. Fingerprint taken from the CI nox-results artifact, not a local scan — they differ. Re-verify if this path ever becomes settable from a request, a plugin manifest, or any other non-operator source.

The limit this rule asks for is set. Both emptyDir volumes added for the read-only root filesystem declare a 64Mi ceiling, which parsing the manifest confirms: the tmp and kubecache volumes each resolve to a mapping carrying that ceiling. The rule matches on the volume-type key alone and does not read the line beneath it, so it reports the ceiling as absent whether it is written inline or below — neither form satisfies it, which is why this is waived rather than restructured. Deliberately worded without reproducing the flagged text, because the rule would then match this reason and file a fresh finding against the baseline itself. Fingerprint taken from the CI nox-results artifact and confirmed identical to a local scan, unlike TAINT-004 above where the two differed. Re-verify if the ceiling is ever removed from either volume, since the finding would then be correct and indistinguishable from this one.
